data.turoyo: Maḥatla u barniṭi b nḥire du dewo, mʕaṭašle lu dewo.
data.translation: und streute dieselbe in die Nase des Wolfes. Der Wolf nieste,

rationale: Second II.1 Preterit example; overt l-coded wolf subject of a bodily event without patient.

data.turoyo: ʕAbər yatu mbalašle šoʕəl w mʕaṭəš w mʕaraṭle.
data.translation: Er kam herein und setzte sich und fing an zu husten und zu niesen und zu furzen.

rationale: Second II.1 Infectum example; complement of beginning in actual narration rather than projected instruction.

summary: Sneezing is intransitive despite II Preterit qṭəlle and overt l-coded subject in PrS 67/31. The L-series does not by itself establish a transitive agent-patient relation.
75/33 is projected speech, 75/35 rehearses a completed sneeze, and 75/38 narrates the event with an Infectum complement of beginning. Temporal interpretation alone does not change the box.
Coughing and breaking wind are coordinated predicates, not evidence of a new sneeze sense or a fixed verb-noun collocation.
The wolf passage gives only a pronoun for the substance strewn into its nose; keep the edition’s same pronoun rather than invent a named stimulus.
